linkedin.name: Eoin Jordan
linkedin.headline: Senior Developer Relations Engineer | Applied Edge AI Research and Developer Education | Agentic AI & MCP | Edge AI | Embedded Systems
linkedin.summary: I research and educate about edge-intelligent systems at the intersection of automation, IoT, and machine learning. I combine research, past experience, and hands-on work to explain how these systems operate in real-world environments. My focus is on systems that actually run in practice — particularly where modern AI tooling must integrate with legacy infrastructure and platforms — and how memory, latency, reliability, deployment, and maintainability shape system design across industrial, automotive, and embedded contexts. I work with a learn-by-doing approach: breaking systems, rebuilding them, then reading deeply to explain why they behave the way they do. Outside software I'm a hands-on automotive mechanic and driving enthusiast (Nürburgring, Mondello Park, Spa-Francorchamps), and I mentor with CoderDojo and Junior Achievement Ireland.

recommendations.name: Ronan Connolly
recommendations.relationship: Worked with Eoin at IBM, on different teams
recommendations.text:
When I first started with IBM Eoin was already an experienced IBMer.

Although he was in a different group to me he really made me feel welcome and thought me the inner workings of IBM and showed me that you need to take it upon yourself to learn, grow, and get initiatives off the ground; instead of relying on the company to do it for you.

He was involved with so many different activities yet still seemed to be getting the daily job done. Some examples were: CoderDojo, IoT Summer School, Various electronics projects, and much more.

Eoin is very passionate about technology and this passion is infectious. If you want to get excited about technology, just hang around with Eoin for a bit!

top_posts.summary: Miniature arcade-machine follow-up to Julian Caro Linares' build on the Arduino UNO Q — concentration tracking with CO2 and an accelerometer, testing traditional control against continuous movement sensing, running on Zephyr.
Rebuilt Clippy as a Zephyr .llext zapp on Jonathan Beri's zephyr-desktop — Qwen Coder plus a RAG index over the real Zephyr docs, hosted on Hugging Face and runnable locally as a coding assistant.

Edge Impulse is now an external module in the Zephyr Project documentation — bringing embedded ML into Zephyr applications as an integrated module, with new west extension commands. Co-authored with Francesco Varani.

highlights: Domain-tuned retrieval for embedded docs: zephyrproject-docs-embeddings and ros2-docs-embeddings, each paired with a base-vs-tuned comparison Space so the gain is measurable, not asserted.
Docs assistants with citations — Zephyr RTOS and ROS 2 coding assistants running retrieval over the real documentation.
Edge AI documentation LoRAs across Qwen2.5-Coder 0.5B / 1.5B / 7B for on-device assistance, plus Arduino + Edge AI combined LoRAs for low-power coding help.
Wake-word tooling end to end: WakeForge generates TTS wake-word datasets, and hey-android-kws / hey-android-piper-kws are the trained classifiers, each with a live demo Space.
Irish-dialect LoRA fine-tuning of Qwen2.5 (irish-abc-qwen2-5-lora) with a ZeroGPU Space.
Public datasets for spark-plug classification and anomaly detection (~3.2k rows combined).
